entries.evidence: Query: "Server-Side Request Forgery Prevention - OWASP Cheat Sheet Series" allow list network layer (cheatsheetseries.owasp.org). Result title 'Server Side Request Forgery Prevention - OWASP Cheat Sheet Series' at this URL; result text: allow lists at application and network layer, validate the resolved IP addresses because a domain allow list does not stop DNS rebinding, deny lists are bypass-prone.
entries.notes: Maps one to one to the D19 defence block (egress policy, address validation, residual risk).

entries.title: OWASP Top 10:2025
entries.access_note: Public OWASP page, indexed without sign-in.
entries.evidence: Query: OWASP Top 10:2025 final release A01 Broken Access Control A05 Injection ... (owasp.org). Result title 'OWASP Top 10:2025' at this URL; result text: A01:2025 Broken Access Control (Server-Side Request Forgery is now part of it), A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration, A05:2025 Injection (third place in 2021), A10:2025 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions. Category pages are also served from top10.owasp.org/2025/.
entries.version: 2025 edition, shown as the current list on 2026-11-18
entries.notes: Version-sensitive for the closed-book classification exam: SSRF is absorbed into A01:2025 Broken Access Control and Injection is A05:2025. The plan does not name an OWASP Top 10 edition for week 4.

entries.title: Releases · juice-shop/juice-shop · GitHub
entries.access_note: Public open-source repository; releases are indexed without sign-in.
entries.evidence: Query: OWASP Juice Shop project page latest release version 2026 companion guide "Pwning OWASP Juice Shop" (owasp.org, github.com, owasp-juice.shop). Result title 'Releases · juice-shop/juice-shop · GitHub' at this URL; result text: v20.4.0 marked latest, assets dated 2026-11-08. Related results: OWASP news 'Juice Shop v20.0.0 - a fresh squeeze of features, now with AI', the OWASP project page (still showing v20.2.0) and 'Running OWASP Juice Shop :: Pwning OWASP Juice Shop' (pwning.owasp-juice.shop/companion-guide/latest/part1/running.html, refers to image v20.3.0).
entries.notes: Local target of the plan: run it only in the isolated VM, bound to loopback, after separate approval; pin the release in the lab record because challenges differ between versions (v20 added AI features). The companion guide contains hints and solutions, so it stays closed during independent blocks. The repository root named in the plan is the parent path of this URL. The estimate is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

entries.title: Overview of HTTP - MDN Web Docs
entries.access_note: Public documentation page, indexed without sign-in.
entries.evidence: Query: MDN "An overview of HTTP" AND "Using HTTP cookies" developer.mozilla.org Web HTTP (developer.mozilla.org). Result title 'Overview of HTTP - MDN Web Docs' at this URL; result text: the protocol is stateless, cookies add sessions. Related results: 'Using HTTP cookies - MDN Web Docs' (.../Web/HTTP/Guides/Cookies, updated about two months ago; an older copy exists at .../Web/HTTP/Cookies) and 'HTTP headers' (.../Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers).
entries.notes: The cookies guide is the reference for the D16 block D inventory (Secure, HttpOnly, Domain and Path).

entries.title: OverTheWire: Natas
entries.access_note: The public page of level 0 (overthewire.org/wargames/natas/natas0.html, search result) publishes the starting user name, password and URL; no registration appears in the results.
entries.evidence: Query: OverTheWire Natas wargame web security server-side natas0 (overthewire.org). Result title 'OverTheWire: Natas' at this URL; result text: 'Natas teaches the basics of serverside web-security'; each level is its own website under natas.labs.overthewire.org and holds the password of the next level; no SSH login.
entries.notes: Free fallback for every independent block of the week. The level topics are not described on the pages seen, so the mapping to days is by level order (early levels for D16). Passwords of levels are spoilers: keep them out of the portfolio. The estimate is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

entries.title: Web Security
entries.access_note: No result on pwn.college stated the access conditions for this dojo module.
entries.evidence: Query: pwn.college "Web Security" module intro-to-cybersecurity path traversal command injection SQL injection challenges (pwn.college). Result title 'Web Security' at this URL; result text: levels Path Traversal 1 and 2, CMDi 1 to 6 (CMDi 5 is blind), SQLi 1 to 5, and in some versions authentication bypass, XSS and same-origin levels. Course copies exist under pwn.college/cse365-f2026/ and older terms with different level lists.
entries.version: as listed 2026-11-18; level lists differ between the dojo and the course copies
entries.notes: Level descriptions seen: Path Traversal 1 is a simple HTTP file server that serves /challenge/files, CMDi 5 is blind, the SQLi levels include a login bypass and a blind leak. Flags and solutions stay out of the portfolio. The estimate is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

plan_fact_checks.claim: OWASP WSTG: the stable documented release is 4.2 (plan section 4 and section 16 item 8).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide latest stable release version v4.2 v5 release 2026 (owasp.org, github.com). Results 'OWASP Web Security Testing Guide' (wstg.owasp.org), the OWASP project page and the OWASP/wstg repository: 'Stable' currently means v4.2; version 5.0 is in development; a pull request 'Publish Latest 2026-10-30' refreshed only the development version.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Versioned WSTG case links are to be preferred to 'latest' (plan section 16 item 8).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Search results show that 'latest' uses another structure and other identifiers than v4.2: the SSRF test is WSTG-INPV-19 under 07-Input_Validation_Testing in v4.2 and WSTG-INJT-19 under 07-Injection in 'latest'; the SQL injection page of 'latest' is at .../07-Injection/05-SQL_Injection/. A 'latest' link therefore breaks or changes meaning over time.

plan_fact_checks.claim: PortSwigger 'All labs' at portswigger.net/web-security/all-labs is the place for exact exercise selection (plan section 4).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query: PortSwigger "mystery lab challenge" web-security mystery-lab-challenge. Result 'All labs' at portswigger.net/web-security/all-labs was returned next to 'Mystery lab challenge'.

plan_fact_checks.claim: D17 block B: two introductory PortSwigger SQL injection labs exist; block C adds one or two more.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Two labs were shown as APPRENTICE ('SQL injection vulnerability in WHERE clause allowing retrieval of hidden data' and 'SQL injection vulnerability allowing login bypass'). Every other SQL injection lab whose level appeared in the results is PRACTITIONER, so the additional labs of block C are one level harder than the plan's wording 'selected' suggests.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Week 4 gate: at least 4 independent labs in at least 2 server-side classes is reachable with introductory labs.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: APPRENTICE labs seen today: SQL injection (2), path traversal (1: simple case), OS command injection (1: simple case), SSRF (2: local server, another back-end system), file upload (1: remote code execution via web shell upload).

plan_fact_checks.claim: OWASP Juice Shop at github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop is the local vulnerable web target (plan section 4).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query: OWASP Juice Shop project page latest release version 2026 ... Result 'Releases · juice-shop/juice-shop · GitHub' under the plan's repository path: v20.4.0 is the latest release (2026-11-08). The OWASP project page still shows v20.2.0 and the companion guide refers to image v20.3.0. The plan pins no version; the lab record should.

plan_fact_checks.claim: D16 block B: Burp Proxy and Repeater can be configured for the labs with the documented free tooling.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query: Burp Suite Community Edition free download limitations Burp Collaborator ... (portswigger.net). Results: 'Download Burp Suite Community Edition' lists the proxy and history, Repeater, Decoder, Sequencer and Comparer in Community, Intruder as a demo, and Burp Collaborator, crawling and scanning as Professional features; release page 'Professional / Community 2026.11' exists. Labs that need Collaborator were therefore left out.

gaps: D20 blocks A and B are an examination and a document review by the plan, so no guided platform exercise is assigned to them. A candidate for a guided review is the TryHackMe room at tryhackme.com/room/owasptopten2025three (OWASP Top 10 2025: Insecure Data Handling, covers A05 Injection); its tier was not seen.

File inclusion (D19): no PortSwigger lab on local or remote file inclusion appeared in the results. The verified options are the TryHackMe room File Inclusion (tier unknown) and the HTB Academy module File Inclusion (Tier II per one search summary, URL academy.hackthebox.com/course/preview/file-inclusion).

No retired Hack The Box machine that is specifically about SQL injection, OS command injection or SSRF was verified; only the Starting Point pages of Sequel and Vaccine were seen, and the pages of Appointment, Crocodile and Oopsie were not returned.
HTB Academy tier not confirmed for SQL Injection Fundamentals, Using Web Proxies and Introduction to Web Applications.
TryHackMe tier not confirmed for Command Injection, File Inclusion and Intro to SSRF.
pwn.college: access conditions of the Web Security module were not shown in a search result.

Defence and detection side of the week (block D): two resources were seen but their tier was not, and they are not recorded as entries: LetsDefend 'Detecting Web Attacks' (app.letsdefend.io/training/lessons/web-attacks-101, covers SQL injection, command injection, RFI and LFI detection) and CyberDefenders 'Web Investigation Lab' (cyberdefenders.org/blueteam-ctf-challenges/web-investigation/, network forensics of a web server compromise).
Out-of-band labs (blind SSRF, blind OS command injection with out-of-band interaction) are not covered because Burp Collaborator is listed as a Professional feature.
Provider-stated durations were not seen for any entry of this week; every estimate is a planning figure.
The shared search budget of the session ended before the TryHackMe room 'Detecting Web Attacks' and the HTB machine pages of Appointment, Dancing, Responder and Archetype could be checked.
